To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novel mutations in the genes that encode the pancreatic beta-cell potassium ATP (KATP) channel, ABCC and KCNJ11 are the most common cause of congenital hyperinsulinaemia (HI), and that in vitro expression studies of the mutations and in vivo phenotyping of family members carrying the same mutation are useful for determining the mode of inheritance and for personalizing management of children with this condition.
in vitro and in silico analyses, together with in vivo carrier phenotypes, are useful tools for interpreting the clinical significance of novel KATP  mutations in patients with congenital HI.
we have described six novel missense mutations in ABCC8 (p.Ala 1458 Thr) and KCNJ11 (p.Ala56Val, p.Asn60Asp, and p.Gly230Arg) in 11 children with congenital hypoglycemic hyperinsulinism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods of gene therapy for congenital diseases.
the development of new therapeutic strategies to treat the most severe forms of diabetes.
the development of new methods for the treatment and prevention of diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the six mutations identified in this study are all dominant pathogenic KATP channel mutations that can cause HI.
these novel missense variants are pathogenic and are likely dominant in nature.
the six mutations are all dominant mutations that can be used to diagnose the HI in the probands and to predict the HI in the family members.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in vitro and in vitro testing is required to identify dominant KATP HI mutations.
the combination of in vitro expression and in vivo phenotype testing can be used to determine whether a KATP channel mutation is a dominant or recessive mutation.
the combination of in vitro expression studies with in vivo phenotype testing is a powerful approach for the diagnosis of dominant KATP channel mutations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in vivo phenotype testing is a valuable tool to determine whether a mutation is dominant or recessive.
in vitro and in vitro studies of KATP channel mutations can be used to predict the clinical phenotype of patients with KATP channel-related HI.
in vitro and in vitro studies can be used to distinguish dominant and recessive mutations.
